facts.text: Director Fred Dekker used little people in alien suits for the opening spaceship scene. He didn't expect the laugh, but thinks it gave the audience permission to laugh for the rest of the movie.
The title credits were designed by Ernie Ferrino, who also worked on The Terminator. Director Fred Dekker asked for a Famous Monsters of Filmland-style logo.
Leslie Ryan, the girl brushing her hair in the black-and-white opening, once turned down a date with writer-director Fred Dekker, who admitted it himself.
Director Fred Dekker wrote the Night of the Creeps script in a single week, stuffing in every B-movie cliche he could think of.
Corman University and the Corman Clarion newspaper are both tributes to B-movie king Roger Corman.
Director Fred Dekker originally wanted to shoot the whole movie in black and white. In the end only the 1959 opening got that treatment.
Night of the Creeps cost about $5 million but grossed just $591,366 in 70 theaters, roughly $3,154 per screen. It became a cult classic on video.
Part of the film was shot inside an old Woolworth's department store converted into a makeshift studio.
Tom Atkins, who plays Detective Ray Cameron, has said Night of the Creeps is his favorite of all the movies he's made.
Director Fred Dekker's roommate, future Lethal Weapon writer Shane Black, helped work on the script.
Tom Atkins himself came up with the idea of having Detective Ray Cameron stop to smell a rose in one scene.
Around the 28-minute mark, Detective Ray Cameron (Tom Atkins) says Whip Van Winkle instead of Rip Van Winkle while mocking the lab break-in. It stayed in the film.
When police mention calling officers Dante and DePalma, it's a nod to directors Joe Dante (Gremlins) and Brian De Palma (Carrie).
Makeup artists Robert Kurtzman, Greg Nicotero and Howard Berger, who later formed KNB EFX, appear in the film as zombie extras.
Effects work came from Howard Berger and Robert Kurtzman, two-thirds of KNB EFX, plus David B. Miller of the Nightmare on Elm Street films. It's all practical, with no CGI.
Spot a second assistant director in the background around 38 minutes, waving onlookers out of frame during the crowd scene.
Director Fred Dekker says Jill Whitlow's top-changing scene was staged to make you wonder whether she'd show nudity, because nudity makes a heroine more vulnerable.
The Stryper Rules graffiti in the men's room exists because makeup artist Kyle Sweet was dating Stryper frontman Michael Sweet, whom she later married.
The tool shed sequence was shot after principal photography wrapped, because test audiences wanted more action.
J.C. (Steve Marshall) is the only infected person who still speaks. Everyone else is zombified instantly because their brains incubate the slugs.
Asked why J.C. uses crutches, director Fred Dekker said there's no reason. A character can be disabled without the story being about it.
Director Fred Dekker says pacing suffered because the studio railroaded him. An executive and the editor recut it without him. After that he carried a stopwatch on every film.
Phil's Diner has become a Fred Dekker signature, turning up somehow in every one of his movies since this one.
Director Fred Dekker and Shane Black wrote Shadow Company, a zombie-soldier script that John Carpenter was to direct with Kurt Russell. It was never made.
The alien spaceship model from this film was later reused in the Star Trek: The Next Generation episode Booby Trap.
For Chris's tape-listening scene, Jason Lively kept clowning. Director Fred Dekker surrounded him with atrocity photos, including Auschwitz, which Lively glances at around 1:04:20.
Jason Lively (Chris) originally auditioned for the role of J.C. He is the brother of actress Blake Lively's half-siblings' family: Blake is his half-sister.
Gordon the cat is named after film producer Gordon Carroll.
Dekker named the Bulldogs football team after his own high school team.
The film was shot with a darker ending, with Detective Ray Cameron zombified and the spaceship returning. It was replaced for theaters and restored in the 2009 DVD and Blu-ray.
Director Fred Dekker received a special first-time-direction award at the 1987 Paris International Festival of Fantastic and Science-Fiction Film.
In the Philippines, early moviegoers got free protector stickers to wear during screenings. In Cincinnati the film was released as Homecoming Night.
German theatrical and VHS releases were cut for violence to get a not-under-16 rating. The cuts were waived on the German Blu-ray.
Director James Wan announced in January 2023 that he wanted to remake Night of the Creeps.
Director Fred Dekker's feature debut was distributed by Tri-Star in 1986. Its makers blamed the poor box office on the studio's lack of promotion.
